description: Exact Claude model IDs pinned per tier for plugin-claude/. HC0-F2: healthcare customers require reproducible behavior — 'opus' or 'sonnet' aliases can drift as Anthropic releases new versions. READ `binding` BELOW BEFORE QUOTING THIS FILE: #519 measured that the pin does not reach a dispatch, so this file records INTENT, not the weights that ran. ./synaptory build copies it into the distribution and the AI-BOM generator reads it.

binding.what_the_pin_controls: Nothing on the dispatch path. The Claude Code Agent() tool's `model` parameter accepts only the tier aliases sonnet|opus|haiku|fable and rejects an exact id with InputValidationError, so the ALIAS is the only value a dispatch can carry and Anthropic's own aliasing resolves it. No file in core/, no hook, and no CLI path reads this file; its readers are markdown prose, the AI-BOM generator, model_pin_check.py and tests.
binding.what_the_pin_is_for: Two things it does deliver. (1) It is the recorded statement of which exact id H3Tech INTENDS each tier to use, shipped in build-metadata.json as ai_bom.model_pins, so a change of intent is a reviewable diff. (2) It is the reference set model_pin_check.py compares an observed receipt against, which is the only automated way drift between intent and observation gets reported.
binding.what_it_is_not: It is NOT evidence of the weights a dispatch ran on, and no auditor or regulated customer may be told a dispatch is reproducible against these ids. What is reproducible is the TIER ROUTING in backends/claude.md Step 2. See #519 and the pinning section of claude.md.
binding.tier_alias_is_a_routing_label: `opus` / `sonnet` / `haiku` are ROUTING labels, not capability guarantees. Nothing here asserts an ordering between the tiers on any measured axis; the cost_tier field states price, which is a published fact, and says nothing about capability. A role is routed to a tier for the reason recorded in that tier's notes, and 'premium' must not be read as 'stronger'.
binding.measurement: Claude Code 2.1.236, 2026-09-03, nine real dispatches (#519 / PR #525). Alias-to-id resolution is a server-side decision that can change on any day and was not measured on Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, or any gateway deployment.

runtime_variants_note: Claude Code surfaces 1M-context variants via suffixes like '-1m' or '[1m]' in the SDK Usage.model field (e.g. 'claude-opus-5-1m'). Per Anthropic's Long-context-pricing policy these variants bill at IDENTICAL per-token rates as the base model — they are NOT separate SKUs. The control-plane pricing logic strips known suffixes before lookup; see api/synaptory_api/routers/analytics.py::_normalise_model_id and ::_PRICED_VARIANT_SUFFIXES. Adding new variants here is informational only; cost computation is automatic once the suffix is in _PRICED_VARIANT_SUFFIXES. A previous PIN is not a runtime variant and must never be listed as one — the two mean different things, and conflating them would make the checker accept an id no dispatch can reach.

decision.reason: The pin named claude-opus-4-8 while every measured dispatch on this tier ran claude-opus-5 (#519 cells A-D and I: subagent dispatches through both the marketplace install and the --plugin-dir sideload, with and without an ambient CLI model default; cell E1 corroborates at session level). Rolling makes the AI-BOM statement true and stops model_pin_check.py refusing the HONEST receipts of five routed roles while staying silent on a forged one — a checker that fires on the honest case and not the dishonest one is worse than none. It changes NO weights: the alias binds and the pin does not, so nothing about the running system moves. It also removes #441's original worry rather than answering it: the premium tier is no longer a generation behind the standard one, because the running system never was — both tiers resolve to the claude-5 generation. Rolling does not restore reproducibility; only a dispatch-mechanism change could, and #519 scoped that out.

opus.notes: Used by the strategic roles (project-owner, solution-architect, compliance-engineer, research-advisor) and, since #434, by code-reviewer; quality-engineer joined in #483. platform-engineer and technical-writer joined later, on a maintainer routing decision recorded in claude.md: neither produces nor proves a work unit, so their tier is free of the decorrelation constraint, and no benchmark here supports reading the move as a quality gain — it is a cost decision. Both provers sit here for weight-level decorrelation, not for seniority: running a work unit's prover on the producer's exact weights makes every judgment-heavy check a same-model check. CR reads diffs; QE decides per-case outcomes for the acceptance set sealed at COMMIT (#406), including whether a case it could not run is legitimately blocked. This is partial decorrelation inside one runtime family; cross-runtime separation is pilot 1 territory and is not wired on the product dispatch path (#396 finding 1). The 1M variants run when Claude Code is configured for >200K context; they bill identically to the base model. A receipt naming claude-opus-4-8 is a finding after this roll, not history: no dispatch on this host was ever measured reaching that id through the `opus` alias (#519 cell E3 reached it only via an explicit session-level --model claude-opus-4-8).

decision.reason: The pin already names the id the alias resolves to (#519 cell E2, session-level --model sonnet). That agreement is a COINCIDENCE, not an enforcement — it is why this whole class of defect stayed invisible for four of nine roles and for the most-dispatched path until #434 moved CR onto `opus`. Nothing to roll to: claude-sonnet-5 is the current sonnet.

sonnet.notes: Used by one role: software-engineer. code-reviewer LEFT this tier in #434, quality-engineer in #483, and the two remaining executor roles (platform-engineer, technical-writer) left for `opus` afterwards on a routing decision that is not about capability — see that tier's notes and the claude.md paragraph. So the producer now sits here alone, which is what makes the prover rows mean anything: a work unit's producing and proving dispatches do not run on identical weights. Do not move either prover back, and do not move software-engineer up, without re-reading those issues. Anthropic ran a $2/$10 per-MTok intro rate through 2026-08-31; the control-plane cost table pins the $3/$15 list rate from 2026-09-01.

decision.reason: The pin names the id the alias resolves to (#519 cell C ran the main session on --model haiku and it reported claude-haiku-4-5). Read the observation_class: that is a SESSION-level measurement, and no synaptory role routes to this tier, so no subagent dispatch has been measured on it. Nothing to roll to either — claude-haiku-4-5 is the current haiku. #434 rejected this tier for a prover on the ground that it is the weaker one; that judgment is recorded there and is not re-derived here.

haiku.notes: Not currently used by synaptory roles; reserved for future low-latency auxiliaries. Anthropic does NOT publish a 1M variant for Haiku 4.5 — treat 'claude-haiku-4-5-1m' model IDs as unsupported.
